title: Cocartesian projection of the relative join with the base
statement: Use simplicial sets, quasicategories, products and degreewise pullbacks of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and cartesian and cocartesian fibrations and their edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Use relative joins and their inclusions from [def-coef-infinity-relative-join]. Let $S,X$ be quasicategories in a fixed universe and let $u:X\to S$ be a cocartesian fibration. Set $Y=X\star_S S$ using $u$ and $\mathrm{id}_S$, and let $\pi:Y\to S$ be the $S$ coordinate of its relative-join pullback. Then $Y$ is a quasicategory, $\pi$ is a cocartesian fibration, and $i_X:X\hookrightarrow Y$ carries every $u$-cocartesian edge to a $\pi$-cocartesian edge.

source.place: Lemma 5.2.3.17 and its cocartesian-edge criterion, specialized to the square with top u:X -> S, bottom identity S -> S, left u and right identity. Compose the resulting fibration to Delta^1 times S with its projection to S; equivalently the opening relative-join construction of Lemma 7.3.4.5 (02ZR). Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: Use the degreewise join summands and block operators of [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone], and unpack the degreewise pullback of [def-coef-infinity-relative-join] with second map $\mathrm{id}_S$. An $m$-simplex of $Y$ is specified uniquely by a base simplex $\sigma\in S_m$, a monotone parameter $\epsilon:[m]\to[1]$, and, if $I=\epsilon^{-1}(0)=[0,k]$ is nonempty, a simplex $a\in X_k$ with $u(a)=\sigma|_I$. Indeed the final join factor is forced to be $\sigma|_{\epsilon^{-1}(1)}$, so it is not additional data. If $I$ is empty the simplex is $i_S(\sigma)$; if $I=[m]$ it is $i_X(a)$ and $u(a)=\sigma$. Faces restrict these data: delete a vertex of $I$ to restrict $a$, delete a final-block vertex to leave $a$ unchanged, and use the pure final-factor simplex when no initial vertex remains. This is exactly the simplicial-operator formula of that definition; it applies also to degeneracies.

source.place: Special-case coordinate calculation for Construction 5.2.3.1, used in Lemma 5.2.3.17. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: We first check when a horn parameter extends. For $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$, every consecutive edge $\{j,j+1\}$ belongs to $\Lambda_i^n$: when $n=2$ these are its two faces, and when $n\geq3$ choose an omitted vertex different from $i,j,j+1$. Thus any map $\Lambda_i^n\to\Delta^1$ assigns a weakly increasing list of vertex values. The resulting monotone $[n]\to[1]$ defines its extension. It agrees on every simplex of the horn, since a simplex of $\Delta^1$ is precisely a monotone list and is determined by its vertices. For $\Lambda_0^n$, $n\geq3$, any edge $\{r,s\}$ omits at least two vertices, so one can choose a vertex $t\notin\{r,s\}$ with $t\neq0$. The present face $d_t$ contains this edge. In particular each consecutive edge is present, so the vertex values are weakly increasing and define the extension, whose restrictions agree with the horn because simplices of $\Delta^1$ are determined by their vertices. For $\Lambda_0^2$, the edges present are $01$ and $02$. If the values at $0,1$ agree, the inequality on $02$ makes the full list monotone. In particular an initial edge lying entirely in either pure factor gives an extension for every $n\geq2$.

source.place: Parameter check in the initial-horn argument of Lemma 5.2.3.16; explicit dimension-two case. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: Here is the mixed-horn calculation, to be reused below. Suppose $h:\Lambda_i^n\to Y$, $n\geq2$, $0\leq i<n$, lies over a specified $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$, and its parameter extends to $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$ with both values occurring. Write $I=[0,k]$ for the zero block, so $k<n$. The face $d_n$ is present because $i\neq n$, and contains all of $I$; its initial-factor datum supplies $a\in X_k$ over $\sigma|_I$. Use $(\sigma,\epsilon,a)$ from Step 1 as the filler. To check each other prescribed face $d_j$, $j\neq i,n$, compare with $d_n$ on their intersection. If $I\setminus\{j\}$ is nonempty, that intersection contains exactly the same initial block as $d_j$, namely $I\setminus\{j\}$ if $j\in I$, and $I$ otherwise. Equality on the intersection therefore forces the initial datum of $d_j$ to be the corresponding restriction of $a$. If that block is empty, $d_j$ has no initial datum. Its other data are already the restrictions of $\sigma$ and $\epsilon$. Thus every prescribed face agrees, hence the filler restricts to all of $h$; the faces and their restrictions cover the horn by its definition. This includes the case $k=n-1$, where $d_n$ is a pure $X$-simplex.

source.place: Explicit mixed case of the lifting arguments in Lemmas 5.2.3.13 and 5.2.3.16. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: To prove that $\pi$ is an inner fibration, take any inner-horn problem over a fixed $\sigma:\Delta^n\to S$. Step 2 extends its parameter. If all parameter values are zero, Step 1 identifies the entire problem with an inner-horn problem for $u:X\to S$, which has a filler since the assumed cocartesian fibration $u$ is an inner fibration by [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. If all values are one, the filler is $i_S(\sigma)$ by Step 1. If both values occur, Step 3 supplies the filler. These cases exhaust the monotone parameters and prove the required right lifting property.

source.place: Special case of Lemma 5.2.3.13, proved directly rather than cited as a theorem. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: Now let an inner horn in $Y$ be given without a specified base filler. Compose it with $\pi$. Since $S$ is a quasicategory, the definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives a base simplex $\sigma$ extending that horn. Step 4 then gives a filler in $Y$ over this $\sigma$. Hence $Y$ is a quasicategory. In particular the inner fibration of Step 4 has quasicategories as both source and target, as required in the definition of cocartesian fibration.

source.place: Quasicategory check needed to interpret the fibration in Lemma 5.2.3.17. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: Let $e:x\to x'$ be a $u$-cocartesian edge. In an arbitrary $\Lambda_0^n$ lifting problem for $\pi$, $n\geq2$, whose edge $01$ is $i_X(e)$, the parameter values at $0,1$ are both zero. Step 2 extends the parameter. If all its values are zero, Step 1 identifies the given horn with an $X$-horn whose initial edge is exactly $e$, and the defining $u$-cocartesian horn property from [def-coef-infinity-fibrations] supplies a filler over the prescribed base simplex. If some value is one, the parameter is mixed and Step 3 supplies a filler. The constant-one case is excluded by the value at $0$. Thus $i_X(e)$ has every defining outer-horn lift and is $\pi$-cocartesian.

source.place: Pure initial-factor edge case of Lemma 5.2.3.16, specialized and proved by horns. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: Every edge $i_S(\alpha)$ in the final factor is $\pi$-cocartesian. Indeed, for any defining $\Lambda_0^n$ problem with initial edge $i_S(\alpha)$, its parameter values at $0,1$ are one. Step 2 gives a monotone extension, necessarily constant one. By Step 1 the entire horn is therefore the final-factor inclusion of its base horn, and $i_S(\sigma)$ for the prescribed base simplex $\sigma$ is a filler. This is precisely the cocartesian-edge criterion in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]; no condition on $\alpha$ is needed.

source.place: Pure final-factor edge case of Lemma 5.2.3.16; explicit specialization to the identity map of S. Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.

proof.text: It remains to produce cocartesian lifts with every prescribed source. By Step 1 in degree zero each vertex of $Y$ is either $i_X(x)$ or $i_S(s)$. For $i_X(x)$ and a base edge $\alpha:u(x)\to t$, the assumed cocartesian fibration $u$ supplies a $u$-cocartesian edge with source $x$ over $\alpha$; its inclusion is $\pi$-cocartesian by Step 6. For $i_S(s)$ and $\alpha:s\to t$, use $i_S(\alpha)$, which is $\pi$-cocartesian by Step 7. Together with Steps 4 and 5 this is exactly the definition of cocartesian fibration in [def-coef-infinity-fibrations]. Step 6 gives the required preservation clause.

source.place: Source-by-source lift construction of Lemma 5.2.3.17; the base projection in the opening of Lemma 7.3.4.5 (02ZR). Direct argument supplied by the worker from the cited definitions, not an application of the general lemma.
